items.title: New warnings on suicide risk from antidepressant medications
items.summary: New safety measures warning about serious side-effects of antidepressant medications, including increased suicidal thoughts and sexual dysfunction, are being introduced by the UK’s drug safety agency.

items.title: ADHD linked to higher odds of early death, but medication may alleviate risk
items.summary: People with ADHD are more likely to die early than those without the condition, but taking the right medication might reduce this risk, a new study has found.

GPs to advise about suicidal behaviour risks when prescribing antidepressants
items.summary: GPs should discuss the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant, the UK medicines regulator has said.

items.title: Mental health nurses to vote on strike action over alleged job cut plans
items.summary: Mental health nurses working at the East London NHS Foundation Trust (ELFT) are being asked to vote on taking strike action as part of a dispute centred on alleged plans to axe hundreds of jobs.

items.title: MHRA announces measures to improve messaging on antidepressant risks
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has announced a series of measures to strengthen messaging around the key risks associated with antidepressant medicines. New boxed warnings will carry information on suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and signpost where patients can get help.

items.title: CQC to regulate all diagnostic assessments for ADHD and autism
items.summary: The Government has asked the CQC to regulate all diagnostic assessments for autism and ADHD, once regulations are in place, following an independent review.

items.title: Can GPs improve ADHD care? And BMA chair on why physician associates should not diagnose patients
items.summary: The new episode of Pulse in Focus: The Podcast for GPs is now live and available on all podcast platforms. In this month’s episode, we look a what the landmark Government-commissioned review into ADHD means for general practice.

GPs should take on long-term ADHD management, landmark review recommends
items.summary: GPs should take on long-term management of ADHD under nationally-mandated shared care arrangements, the landmark Government review into ADHD and autism has recommended.

items.title: Nurse-led review reveals themes in suicide compensation claims
items.summary: Lack of family engagement is among the recurring themes in compensation claims against the NHS involving a patient suicide, a national review led by a nurse has found.

items.title: Infant feeding and mental health support to be rolled out across England by 2028
items.summary: A ‘Healthy Babies’ programme like what used to be provided in Sure Start centres will be rolled out to all local authorities by 2028, the Government has announced.

items.title: Hospitals paid up to ten times more than GPs to monitor adult ADHD patients, LMC claims
items.summary: Exclusive GP leaders in one area have claimed they have been offered ten times less than hospitals to deliver the same ADHD service.

items.title: First occupational mental health nurse for Northern Irish trust
items.summary: A health and social care trust in Northern Ireland has appointed a mental health nurse to its occupational health team for the first time.

items.title: Willingness to seek help may explain rising mental health demand among young people
items.summary: An increase in demand for GP appointments for mental health issues may be down to a greater willingness among young people to seek help, a study has found. Norwegian researchers said mental health problems have being reported to have risen in many high-income countries, particularly among teens and young adults.
